data.name: Jalu
data.gender_notes: Jalu is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Jalu is derived from the Sanskrit word ‘jal’, meaning water or wave. In Hindu mythology, Jalu is a name of Lord Shiva, symbolizing the gentle and powerful flow of the universe. The name Jalu carries the meaning “Gentle Wave” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Jalu usually hope their child will grow to embody gentle wave and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbolizes the gentle and powerful flow of the universe.
data.etymology: Jalu belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Gentle Wave.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Jalu total 8, giving a life-path number of 8. Number 8 is linked with Saturn and with the qualities of ambition, resilience and material success.

data.spiritual_symbolism: The name Jalu is derived from the Sanskrit word 'jala', meaning 'water'. In Hinduism, water represents purity, life, and the divine force that sustains all creation. Therefore, the name Jalu signifies a pure soul, one who is connected to the divine source and nurtures the life within them and around them.

historical_references.reference: Jalu Shah was a ruler of the Sisodia Rajput clan and the 13th Maharaja of Mewar. He ruled from 1458 to 1473.
Jalu Ode is mentioned in the Maratha records of the 17th century as the head of the Jajpur Zamindari in Orissa. He was a vassal of the Mughal Emperor Akbar.

modern_usage.modern_context: The name Jalu is of Hindu origin and its modern context is often associated with vibrant and colorful fashion trends. Jaluritis refer to traditional Indian necklaces with the name Jalu incorporated into the design. Jaluponga is a term used to describe a modern take on the traditional Indian saree, where the fabric is wrapped and tied in a unique way to resemble a pompom, creating a fun and trendy look. Jalushi is a popular term used on social media platforms such as TikTok and Instagram, representing individuals who embody the modern and colorful spirit of the Jalu name. These trends reflect the fusion of traditional culture with modern fashion, showcasing the versatility and adaptability of the Hindu name Jalu.
